INDAPT is the brand under which we develop digital products, create IT solutions and help businesses improve their technology and communications. Through the INDAPT website at indapt.net, we introduce our work, publish materials and receive enquiries about working together.

These Terms of Use set out the rules for using the INDAPT website, its materials and general communication channels. Individual projects are agreed separately. Our Privacy Policy explains personal data, cookies and privacy choices.
Working together under the INDAPT brand

INDAPT brings together an entrepreneurial approach, collaborative working and shared professional principles. Different companies, independent specialists and partners may participate in projects. The participants are selected according to the task, required expertise, country and region of delivery.

The service provider, contracting party, representatives' authority and allocation of responsibilities are determined for each engagement. A shared name, corporate culture, email domain or presentation of a team on the website does not, by itself, authorise each participant to make commitments for everyone else.

Contractual obligations belong to the persons that properly undertake them. Participation in a shared team does not automatically create joint liability, an agency relationship or authority to act for another participant. This does not exclude responsibility arising under law or a separate agreement.
The purpose of the website

The website helps you learn about INDAPT, assess our experience and start a discussion. It is intended primarily for a professional business audience. Service and capability descriptions indicate possible areas of work; the appropriate solution is determined after considering the particular task.

Publishing a service, case study, preliminary estimate or presentation does not, by itself, constitute a public offer or commit anyone to delivering any project on those terms. The express terms of a particular offer may provide otherwise.

Sending an enquiry does not conclude a contract, reserve a team or start paid work. Fees, timescales, deliverables, acceptance, development rights, support and warranties are agreed in the project documents.
What these Terms cover

These Terms concern the public pages of the INDAPT website, their materials and general enquiry forms. A particular service, account area, event or digital product may have additional terms available before it is used.

A project contract, confidentiality agreement and agreed data processing terms govern the relevant engagement within their scope. These general website Terms do not amend them or override mandatory law. Where provisions differ, the document governing the particular issue applies, taking account of its terms and applicable law.
Using website materials

You may read materials, share links and retain extracts for personal reference or internal assessment of working together. Keep attribution and source information when retaining materials. Statutory quotation rights and other lawful exceptions remain available.

Publishing text, designs, illustrations, videos, presentations, software elements or other work does not transfer intellectual property rights. The rights holder may be an INDAPT participant, author, client or another person. Rights in all displayed materials should not be attributed to a single participant.

Republication of complete materials, commercial redistribution, design adaptation, use of brand assets or incorporation into your own product requires appropriate permission unless permitted by law or a published licence. Send requests to hello@indapt.net.
Links and representations of a relationship with INDAPT

You may provide an accurate link to a public website page. It must lead to the actual material and must not falsely suggest that INDAPT endorses your activities, is a party to your offer or guarantees its outcome.

You must not present the website or its parts as your own resource, conceal the origin of materials or use the design and name in a way that falsely presents an external resource as an official INDAPT channel. Logo use and representations of an official partnership require a separate basis.

Client, platform, media, industry association and technology company names belong to their respective rights holders. A reference may describe experience, an integration, a publication or another context. A particular relationship status depends on the relevant agreement or programme and is not established merely by displaying a name or logo.
Sending an enquiry or proposal

To understand a task, we may need your contact details, organisation name, project description and working materials. Provide information you are entitled to share and a contact for our response. Anyone approaching us for an organisation should have the appropriate authority.

Materials are considered in connection with the matter you raise: to clarify the task, assess possible involvement, prepare a response and agree next steps. Receiving a proposal does not create an obligation to accept it, enter a tender or pay for materials you have prepared without a separate agreement.

Do not send passwords, access keys, payment card details, identity documents, sensitive personal data or restricted information through a general form. First agree whether such information is needed, a secure channel and the permitted recipients.
Briefs and confidential information

Rights in submitted materials remain with the relevant rights holders. Sending a brief or idea does not authorise its publication, unrelated disclosure or independent commercial exploitation. Use is limited to what is necessary to consider the enquiry and carry out agreed work, on a lawful basis.

General communication channels are intended for an initial discussion. Before disclosing trade secrets, unpublished developments, client data or other sensitive information, agree the confidentiality arrangements, participants' authority and access conditions.

Preliminary correspondence does not replace specifically agreed trade secret arrangements or a confidentiality agreement. The absence of such an agreement does not remove duties already imposed by law or permit arbitrary disclosure of received information.
Publications and project results

We aim to present information accurately and in a clear context. Technologies, interfaces, external platform prices and solution requirements change. A publication may describe experience as at its publication date rather than the current availability of every tool.

Case study metrics relate to a particular project, period and set of circumstances. They may depend on starting information, budget, client involvement, market conditions and external services. One project's outcome does not guarantee the same result for another. Binding metrics and acceptance criteria are agreed in the contract.

Articles, reviews and expert commentary provide general information. Decisions affecting security, law, finance or a particular system's architecture require assessment of the relevant circumstances. You may ask us to clarify the context of published material.
International work and technology choices

The ability to provide a service or use a platform depends on the country, project participants, data requirements, tool availability and applicable restrictions. The permissible scope is established for the particular circumstances before the relevant commitments are made.

References to international experience, partners or technologies do not mean that every service is available in every country or that every INDAPT participant has a local establishment, licence or special status in that jurisdiction.

Selecting a website language does not change mandatory legal requirements or authorise conduct restricted by applicable law. Using an external platform does not remove project participants' data protection duties or obligations to observe applicable restrictions.
External websites and digital services

The website may link to resources operated by other owners. Once you follow a link, the relevant owner's terms govern that resource. A link is not, by itself, confirmation of all its content or a guarantee of its security.

An embedded video player, map, form or other external element may process technical information before you visit a separate website. Enabling these functions and the relevant user choices are addressed by our Privacy Policy and the relevant service's terms.

We remain responsible for our own conduct under applicable law. The circumstances of integrating or recommending an external service are assessed separately; an external link does not, by itself, remove statutory responsibility.
Acceptable and secure use

Do not seek access to other people's information or restricted areas, bypass controls, interfere with website operation, distribute malicious files, send spam or knowingly false messages. Forms must not be used to infringe other people's rights or unlawfully distribute information.

Automated collection must not bypass technical protections, infringe content rights, obtain personal data without a lawful basis or impose a disproportionate load. Ordinary indexing of public pages is permitted subject to published technical restrictions and law.

If you discover a vulnerability, email hello@indapt.net with the page and circumstances. Do not access other people's information or publish details in a way that enables harm before the issue is resolved.
Website availability

We may update pages, change functions or temporarily restrict access for maintenance or protection. We may also restrict actions threatening security, breaching law or infringing other people's rights. Such measures should be proportionate to the issue.

A public information website does not carry a separate commitment to uninterrupted access or continued availability of every material. Where availability, support or recovery times have been agreed for a project, those contractual arrangements apply.
If a page or form is inaccessible to you for technical reasons, email hello@indapt.net. Where possible, we will offer another way to obtain the information or send an enquiry.
Responsibility

Each participant is responsible for its own conduct and undertaken obligations under law and applicable agreements. These Terms do not release a participant from responsibility imposed by law, a data processing arrangement or a contract.

Claims concerning the public information website are assessed by reference to the breach, causation and substantiated loss. To the extent permitted by law, the website does not establish an entitlement to compensation for anticipated profit or commercial opportunities merely because a visitor expected a publication to remain unchanged, an external service to remain available or a case study result to be repeated.

Limitations do not apply where prohibited by law. They do not exclude liability for intentional wrongdoing, fraud, breaches of mandatory user rights or personal data protection duties. Where applicable law prohibits limiting liability for death, personal injury or other matters, those limitations do not apply either.
Corrections and concerns

If material affects your rights, contains an inaccuracy or unlawfully uses a work, image or personal data, email hello@indapt.net with the link, explanation and a contact for our response. If acting for a rights holder, explain your authority. Do not attach unnecessary documents containing personal data.

We consider the circumstances and, where justified, correct, restrict or remove material. Our Privacy Policy describes personal data requests and deadlines. Contacting us does not limit your right to use remedies provided by law.
Applicable legislation

Interactions with users and project delivery are governed by the applicable laws of the relevant countries, including mandatory local rules. The terms of cooperation for each project are agreed separately by the parties in accordance with those requirements.
Effect of these Terms and updates
The Russian and English versions convey the same meaning. Interface language alone does not select a governing law or waive statutory rights.
If a provision is inapplicable or invalid, the remaining provisions continue to apply to the extent permitted. Not exercising a right on one occasion does not automatically waive it for the future.

We update these Terms as the website and its requirements develop. The month and year of the latest update appear above. Changes do not retrospectively revise past actions, undertaken obligations or an existing project contract.
For website, content and business enquiries: hello@indapt.net.
